🖥 Minister calls for promoting equity in Iran’s public education

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Education Minister Alireza Kazemi, emphasizing educational equity, says that creating equal learning opportunities and standardizing educational, developmental, and sports facilities remain among the country’s core policies.

Kazemi made the remarks during a ceremony at Parvin Etesami Elementary School in the city of Baharestan to mark the start of the new academic year, coinciding with the martyrdom anniversary of Hazrat Fatemeh Masoumeh (SA).
​
Pointing to the disparity in per-capita educational facilities in certain regions, he said the areas lacking educational space must be brought up to minimum standards by completing the unfinished projects.
​
Kazemi stated that the projects already completed to 80-90 percent must be given priority and their execution should be taken seriously.
​
He also underscored the importance of expanding on-campus sports facilities, noting that artificial turf fields, sports halls, and school gymnasiums require attention, including an increased investment in sports programs for girls.
​
The minister also announced expansion of academic spaces, saying that through the efforts of philanthropists, the public, and various agencies, the country’s educational capacity has expanded by 24,000 classrooms across 4,700 educational facilities.
​
Elsewhere in his remarks, Kazemi paid tribute to the martyrs of the Islamic Revolution and the Sacred Defense, including students and teachers, stating that the country’s youth would fulfill their mission of serving the nation, pursuing knowledge, and maintaining steadfastness and resistance.
​
Addressing the students, he said the country’s future lies in their hands; and through hard work, the pursuit of knowledge, faith, and determination, they can reach the pinnacles of scientific achievement.
​
During the event that was attended by various provincial and local officials, including the Governor of Baharestan and the member of parliament representing the Baharestan County, 3,000 livelihood assistance packages were distributed among needy students.
